[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"CSRF Protection and Security Headers in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web security is a critical aspect of application development. In this tutorial, you will learn how to secure your Flask application against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks and how to implement essential HTTP security headers using Flask-WTF and Flask-Talisman."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before we begin, ensure you have Flask, Flask-WTF, and Flask-Talisman installed in your Python environment. You can install these packages using pip."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install Flask Flask-WTF Flask-Talisman"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing CSRF Protection"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cross-Site Request Forgery occurs when a malicious website causes a user's web browser to perform an unwanted action on a trusted site where they are currently authenticated. Flask-WTF provides built-in CSRF protection for your forms and routes."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask, render_template, request, redirect, url_for
from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = "your-very-secure-secret-key"

csrf = CSRFProtect(app)

@app.route("/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def index():
    if request.method == "POST":
        return "CSRF token validated successfully!"
    return render_template("index.html")"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Adding CSRF Tokens to Templates"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"When using Flask-WTF, you must include the hidden CSRF token in all of your HTML forms. If you are using standard HTML forms instead of WTForms, you can still render the token manually."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"<form method="POST">
    <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}"/>
    <label for="username">Username:</label>
    <input type="text" id="username" name="username">
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Security Headers with Flask-Talisman"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"HTTP security headers instruct the browser on how to behave when handling your application content. Flask-Talisman is an extension that handles HTTPS redirection and sets security headers like Content Security Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, and Strict-Transport-Security out of the box."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from flask_talisman import Talisman

app = Flask(__name__)

# Basic Talisman configuration
talisman = Talisman(app)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Customizing Content Security Policy (CSP)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"A robust Content Security Policy restricts the domains from which scripts, images, and other resources can be loaded. You can pass a custom CSP dictionary to Flask-Talisman to fine-tune these permissions."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"csp = {
    "default-src": "'self'",
    "script-src": ["'self'", "https://trustedscripts.com"],
    "style-src": ["'self'", "https://trustedstyles.com"]
}

talisman = Talisman(app, content_security_policy=csp)"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always keep your SECRET_KEY complex and secret, ideally loaded from an environment variable."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable CSRF protection globally using Flask-WTF across all state-changing routes (POST, PUT, DELETE)."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Flask-Talisman to automatically enforce HTTPS and inject standard security headers."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test your application headers using online security scanners to ensure proper deployment."}]
